svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Material Standards

g.text: Particleboard only where the building is built in
a factory, so the subfloor is not exposed to the
weather, (2). Grade D-2 or D-3, ANSI A208.1, (3)
Treated to restrict water absorption in bathrooms,
kitchens, laundry rooms or other areas subject

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as provided in Sentence (2), wood-based
panels for subfloors conform to
(a) CSA O121, "Douglas fir plywood" (b) CSA O151,
"Canadian softwood plywood" (c) CSA O153, "Poplar
plywood" (d) CSA O325, "Construction sheathing,"
or (e) CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard."
Particleboard subflooring may be used only
where a building is constructed in a factory
so that the subfloor will not be exposed to
the weather.
Subflooring described in Sentence (2) conforms
to grade D-2 or D-3 in ANSI A208.1,
"Particleboard."
Subflooring described in Sentence (2) has its
upper surface and all edges treated to
restrict water absorption, where the subfloor
is used in bathrooms, kitchens, laundry rooms
or other areas subject to periodic wetting.
Drawn: swatch faces and the factory and room pictograms are illustration only. Treated surfaces in B in light blue.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.15.2. (page 9-223)
